Networking, environment variables and secrets

Follow the website-to-API and API-to-database connections using service names.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A student website, API and database running in containers

Package a .NET API and MVC website into images. Docker Compose starts them with SQL Server so the three services can work together.

SQL Server stores its files in a named Docker volume so they can survive container replacement.

Check the result

Follow the setup steps, start the Compose stack, open the website and add a student.

Containers have their own idea of localhost. Service names are the addresses they use to talk to one another on the Compose network.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Prepare your computer

Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers enabled and the .NET10 SDK. For the full SQL Server stack use supported x64 hardware with enough memory for SQL Server. WPF does not run in the Linux ASP.NET image. Accept applicable vendor licences yourself during installation. Run docker version and docker compose version in a terminal; start Docker Desktop if the engine cannot be reached.

Map the addresses

  • Browser on your computer → localhost:5200 → website container port8080.
  • Website server → http://api:8080/ → API container. This is server-to-server HTTP, so browser CORS does not apply to that internal hop.
  • API → Server=db,1433 → SQL Server. The database port is not published to the host in this sample.
  • ConnectionStrings__School maps to ConnectionStrings:School in ASP.NET configuration. Environment variables can override appsettings.json.
  • The .env file helps Compose substitute values. It is not an encrypted vault. Docker inspect/config output can reveal environment values. Use managed secrets and a least-privilege database account for production.

Common mistakes

LEFA\SQLEXPRESS is a Windows host instance name, not the address of the db container. Host port5100 and container port8080 have different jobs. Bind practice published ports to127.0.0.1 to avoid exposing the lab on every network interface. Inside containers, use service names; outside, use the published localhost port.

Try it yourself

Website cannot reach localhost:5100 from its container. Fix the URL.

Worked answer

Set SchoolApi to http://api:8080/. The API is another container on the Compose network.

Can a password be safe just because .env is hidden?

Worked answer

No. It is plaintext. Keep it out of Git, logs and screenshots, and use proper secret management for deployment.
